t: You're standing by St Martin-in-the-Fields, the church at the north-east corner of Trafalgar Square. It's named for Saint Martin of Tours, and there has been a church on this site since at least the medieval period, when this was farmland beyond the London wall. Several notable people are buried here. Robert Boyle is often regarded as the first modern chemist. The mathematician Abraham de Moivre lies here too. So does Nell Gwyn, the Restoration actress. The furniture designer Thomas Chippendale is buried here, and so is the miniaturist Nicholas Hilliard, who painted the courts of Elizabeth I and James I.
